quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What driving technique helps prevent crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highway as soon as possible.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snowy or icy roads. Slowing down and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right and stop.
Stop where you are right now.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill is coming up.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal first, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do all of these before moving to the new lane.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and other vehicles is important because it:

options.text: Gives you time to react if something unexpected happens.
Keeps traffic moving at safe speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if something unexpected happens.
questions.explanation: Leaving plenty of space between you and other vehicles gives you enough time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: If someone has drunk alcohol, what will help them overcome its effects?
questions.explanation: Only time will let alcohol leave a person's body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: The most effective safety restraints in a crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chances of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injuries. Airbags used with safety belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the road:

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you don't scare or startle it.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-lane road unless:

options.text: You can see the road clearly ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: Safe passing on a two-lane road requires three things: you can see the road ahead clearly, you can get back to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn on your signal and check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and make sure no one is moving into the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What can you do in the center lane?
questions.explanation: This lane is only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight through.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:
questions.explanation: In rain, always use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, you should:

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to where you came from.
Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers position their vehicles correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming hazards.

questions.question: To drive safely based on your physical condition, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. Know your limits and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. You should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Turn on flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the wheel tightly and stay in your lane. Let off the gas slowly, then brake lightly. Pull safely off the road.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Usually slows your reaction to hazards.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows your reaction to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow how fast you can react to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is always unsafe.

questions.question: Passing is not allowed:
questions.explanation: You cannot pass on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These areas are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: Car crashes are most often caused by:
questions.explanation: Most crashes are caused by what drivers do or do not do. Safe driving is your responsibility.
